issues.failure_explanation: With the paper's sign convention (Delta_y Phi = delta, hence the interior/boundary kernel integrals equal 1 and 1/2), the interior trace of the double-layer potential is (1/2)beta(x*) + \int beta \partial_{n_y}\Phi(x*,y) d\sigma_y, which is exactly what the (correct) BIE (BIE) encodes. The displayed formula (BIE-limit) instead equates the limit with u(x*) - (1/2)beta(x*) = f(x*) - (1/2)beta(x*), which is false: on the unit disc with psi = 0 and beta identically 1 (so f identically 1), the left side equals 1 while the right side equals 1/2. As written, the 'Hence' step deriving the BIE does not follow from (BIE-limit).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we see that the errors decrease monotonically (though not necessarily strictly) with the number of hidden layers. This result is explainable given the results of Theorem \ref{error-bounds-thrm}

issues.failure_explanation: For the unit-disc Poisson BIE (poisson-ex) the kernel is the constant 1/(4 pi), so the fixed-point operator is T beta = 2g - (1/(2 pi)) \int_0^{2 pi} beta d\theta, and for a constant difference beta_1 - beta_2 = c one gets ||T beta_1 - T beta_2||_\infty = |c| = ||beta_1 - beta_2||_\infty. Hence no q < 1 satisfies the non-expansiveness inequality: the best constant is q = 1. At q = 1 the invoked bound (fnn-error) has prefactor e^{1-q}/(1-q) = +\infty and decay factor e^{-(1-q)v_M} = 1, so it yields no finite, M-decaying estimate of ||beta - beta_M||. The same holds for the Krasnoselskii-Mann averaged operator implemented by the Fredholm NN, whose best sup-norm Lipschitz constant is also 1. Thus in the regime of the paper's Poisson forward example (ex1) and Poisson inverse example (inv-ex), Theorem error-bounds-thrm delivers only a vacuous bound, and the monotone-decay explanation offered in Section explainability is not supported by the cited theory (the iteration does converge geometrically, but for spectral reasons not captured by (fnn-error)).

failure_location.quote: where $\left\|\beta - \beta_M \right\|_{\partial \Omega}$ is the error in the  FNN approximation of the boundary function $\beta$, as given in (\ref{fnn-error}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a convergence-rate analysis of the relaxed fixed-point iteration for the disc Poisson BIE operator (e.g., diagonalizing the averaged operator in the Fourier basis on the circle, which gives geometric decay with rate max(|1-2 kappa|, 1-kappa) despite q = 1), or explicitly restrict the quantitative error-bound claims to the strictly contractive regime q < 1 (which holds for the Helmholtz cases).
issues.overall_effect: For the unit-disc Poisson problems — the forward example and the inverse-source example — the advertised explicit, decaying a priori error bounds of Theorem error-bounds-thrm are vacuous, and the explainability claims resting on them (and the abstract's 'explicit error bounds' claim) are unsupported in that regime. The Helmholtz-based results (lambda > 0, including the recurrent scheme, where the kernel gives q < 1) are unaffected, and the numerical scheme itself still converges.
issues.title: Invoked FNN bound (fnn-error) is vacuous for the disc Poisson BIE (best constant q = 1)
issues.why_classification: Restoring quantitative bounds for the disc-Poisson regime requires a genuinely new but contained argument (a spectral/rate lemma whose ingredients — the explicit constant kernel and the KM structure — are in the source), or a limited restriction of the advertised claims to lambda > 0; convergence and the numerics survive, but the advertised explicit decaying bound for the Poisson examples is currently unsupported.

But D\Phi(x,y) = \partial_{n_y}\Phi(x,y) - \partial_{n_y}\Phi(x*,y) is a difference and changes sign already on the unit disc (it is the Poisson kernel minus 1/(4 pi); \int D\Phi = 1/2 while \int |D\Phi| grows to 3/2 near the boundary). Hence the constant 2||\int D\Phi d\sigma_y||_\Omega appearing in (error-domain) is not established; the valid estimate uses the strictly larger 2||\int |D\Phi| d\sigma_y||_\Omega, and for worst-case error profiles the stated constant can be exceeded. The same device in the 4th term requires \partial_{n_y}\Phi \ge 0, which holds on the disc (and on convex domains) but not for the general geometries the paper claims to cover, while the theorem states no geometric restriction.

The structure of the bounds, the decay in ||beta - beta_M||, and all qualitative conclusions are unchanged.
issues.title: Sup-norm pulled inside a signed kernel integral in the error-bounds-thrm proof
issues.why_classification: The repair is local and routine (absolute values or a convexity restriction); the form of the bounds, the decay structure, and every qualitative claim survive, with only a larger but still fully explicit constant.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \State {Step 1. Construct the PDE (\ref{iteration}) with source term $\psi_n(x) := -\lambda u_n(x) + F(x,u_n(x))$.}

issues.failure_explanation: Per Algorithm alg:nl-algo, \tilde u_n is computed from the source -lambda \tilde u_{n-1} + F(., \tilde u_{n-1}), so it approximates T(\tilde u_{n-1}), not the exact iterate u_n = T(u_{n-1}). Hence ||\tilde u_n - u_n|| is not bounded by the single-solve PFNN error (error-domain) unless u_n is redefined as T(\tilde u_{n-1}) — but then the 'known error bound for the fixed point iterations', ||u_n - u|| \le q^n ||u_0 - u||, no longer applies, since that estimate holds only for the exact iteration. The recursion the algorithm actually satisfies is e_n \le \epsilon^{RPFNN}_\Omega + q e_{n-1}, giving ||\tilde u_n - u||_\Omega \le \epsilon^{RPFNN}_\Omega (1 - q^n)/(1 - q) + q^n ||u_0 - u||_\Omega, which exceeds the stated bound \epsilon^{RPFNN}_\Omega + q^n ||u_0 - u||_\Omega for every n \ge 2 and q > 0 (e.g., q = 1/2, n = 2 gives a factor 1.5 on \epsilon). The boundary bound in (error-recurrent) survives, since each exact linear solve attains f on the boundary, so no accumulation occurs there (the stated boundary bound is merely conservative).

failure_location.quote: Notice that we can decompose the error into a component arising from the fixed point iterations and another due to the neural network approximation by writing $\left\|\tilde{u}_n - u \right\|_{\Omega} \leq \left\|\tilde{u}_n - u_n \right\|_{\Omega} + \left\|u_n - u \right\|_{\Omega}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the interior bound as ||\tilde u_n - u||_\Omega \le \epsilon^{RPFNN}_\Omega (1 - q^n)/(1 - q) + q^n ||u_0 - u||_\Omega and prove it by induction from the recursion e_n \le \epsilon^{RPFNN}_\Omega + q e_{n-1}.
issues.overall_effect: The interior error bound in (error-recurrent) for the Recurrent PFNN understates the true a priori error: the single-solve PFNN error is amplified by the geometric factor (1 - q^n)/(1 - q) (up to 1/(1 - q)), so the advertised interior bound can be violated for n \ge 2. No other labelled result depends on the lemma.
issues.title: Recurrent PFNN error bound omits accumulation of per-iteration PFNN errors
issues.why_classification: The stated bound is false as written; the forced correction weakens the advertised guarantee by the factor (1 - q^n)/(1 - q) on the PFNN-error term — a limited weakening that preserves the qualitative result (geometric convergence to an error floor) but withdraws the stronger stated bound.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \frac{\partial \Phi(x,y)}{\partial n_y} = -\frac{\sqrt{\lambda} K_0' \left( \sqrt{\lambda} |x - y| \right)}{2\pi |x - y|} \big( y_1 (y_1 - x_1) + y_2 (y_2 - x_2) \big).

issues.failure_explanation: On the unit circle y\cdot(y - x) = 1 - cos(theta_1 - theta_2) = |x - y|^2/2, so the kernel is \partial_{n_y}\Phi(x,y) = sqrt(lambda) |x - y| K_1(sqrt(lambda) |x - y|) / (4 pi), which has the diagonal limit 1/(4 pi) that the paper itself derives. The printed closed form sqrt(lambda) K_1(sqrt(lambda)|x-y|) / (4 pi |x-y|) is off by a factor |x - y|^{-2}: it does not follow from the preceding general formula (whose denominator is |x - y|, not |x - y|^2), it diverges like |x - y|^{-2} as y -> x (a non-integrable singularity, contradicting the paper's own weak-singularity treatment and diagonal value), and it is inconsistent with the lambda -> 0 limit 1/(4 pi).

failure_location.quote: \frac{\partial \Phi(x,y)}{\partial n_y} = \frac{\sqrt{\lambda} K_1 \left( \sqrt{\lambda} |x - y| \right)}{2\pi |x - y|^2} \left( y_1 (y_1 - x_1) + y_2 (y_2 - x_2) \right) = \frac{\sqrt{\lambda} K_1 \left( \sqrt{\lambda} |x - y| \right)}{4\pi |x - y|}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the closed-form kernel by the correct expression sqrt(lambda) |x - y| K_1(sqrt(lambda) |x - y|) / (4 pi) (with diagonal value 1/(4 pi)), which follows directly from the paper's own preceding general formula.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed kernel is the formula the paper presents as the basis for numerically constructing the Helmholtz BIE; as printed it would produce an incorrect, singularly behaved discretization. No formal result depends on the formula, but the claim of a complete numerical construction for the Helmholtz kernel is misleading, and if the printed formula were actually used, the reported Helmholtz numerical results would be compromised.
issues.title: Incorrect closed-form Helmholtz double-layer kernel on the unit circle
issues.why_classification: The correction is a single forced, local recomputation; no theorem uses the formula and the diagonal asymptotics actually used to handle the singularity are correct, so every formal claim survives once the display is fixed.
